---
title: "Fit model"
sidebar: start
---

Once a function is defined declaring the model, you can fit the model to the data using the ```fit``` function. By default `fit()` runs the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) with 4 chains of 1000 warm-up and 1000 sampling iterations, using the data stored in `m.data_on_model` (filled by `m.data()` / `m.data_to_model()` or assigned directly).

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Python
``` python
from BayesForge import bf

m = bf(platform="cpu")
m.data(m.load.howell1(only_path=True), sep=";")
m.df = m.df[m.df.age > 18]
m.scale(["weight"])

def model(weight, height):
    a = m.dist.normal(178, 20, name="a")
    b = m.dist.log_normal(0, 1, name="b")
    s = m.dist.uniform(0, 50, name="s")
    m.dist.normal(a + b * weight, s, obs=height)

m.fit(model)  # Optimize model parameters through MCMC sampling
m.summary()
```
## R
``` R
library(BayesForge)

m <- importBF(platform = "cpu")
m$data(m$load$howell1(only_path = TRUE), sep = ";")
m$df <- m$df[m$df$age > 18, ]
m$scale(list("weight"))
m$data_to_model(list("weight", "height"))

model <- function(height, weight) {
    a <- bf.dist.normal(178, 20, name = "a")
    b <- bf.dist.log_normal(0, 1, name = "b")
    s <- bf.dist.uniform(0, 50, name = "s")
    bf.dist.normal(a + b * weight, s, obs = height)
}

m$fit(model) # Optimize model parameters through MCMC sampling
m$summary()
```
## Julia
``` julia
using PyBayesForge

m = importBF(platform = "cpu")
m.data(m.load.howell1(only_path = true), sep = ';')
m.df = m.df[m.df.age > 18]
m.scale(["weight"])

@BF function model(weight, height)
    a = m.dist.normal(178, 20, name = 'a')
    b = m.dist.log_normal(0, 1, name = 'b')
    s = m.dist.uniform(0, 50, name = 's')
    m.dist.normal(a + b * weight, s, obs = height)
end

m.fit(model)  # Optimize model parameters through MCMC sampling
m.summary()
```
:::

## Main arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | — | The model function. Its arguments are matched by name to the entries of `m.data_on_model`. |
| `obs` | `None` | Optional dictionary of data; replaces `m.data_on_model` for this fit. |
| `num_warmup` | `1000` | Warm-up (adaptation) iterations per chain; discarded. |
| `num_samples` | `1000` | Posterior draws kept per chain. |
| `num_chains` | `4` | Number of chains. |
| `chain_method` | `"parallel"` | `"parallel"` (one device per chain), `"vectorized"` or `"sequential"`. |
| `thinning` | `1` | Keep every *n*-th draw. |
| `target_accept_prob` | `0.8` | NUTS target acceptance rate; raise (e.g. `0.95`) when there are divergences. |
| `max_tree_depth` | `10` | Maximum NUTS tree depth. |
| `dense_mass` | `False` | Use a dense (full-covariance) mass matrix. |
| `progress_bar` | `True` | Show a progress bar. |
| `seed` | `None` | Explicit sampler seed; by default derived from `rand_seed` (see [Random and fixed seeds](Random and fixed seeds.qmd)). |

After fitting, posterior draws are in `m.posteriors` (a dictionary of arrays), and `m.summary()` returns the posterior summary table.
